papers.title: Photocurable Allyl-Succinylated Collagen Bioink for High-Resolution 3D Bioprinting and Regenerative Diabetic Wound Healing.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting of collagen-based hydrogels remains limited by poor solubility, weak mechanics, and slow photocrosslinking, which hinder print fidelity and restrict clinical translation. Here, we report a photocurable allyl-succinylated collagen (CAA) bioink that overcomes these long-standing challenges by integrating enhanced molecular solubility, rapid photocrosslinkability, and intrinsic bioactivity. The allyl-succinyl modification markedly improved collagen solubility and enabled efficient radical-mediated polymerization, yielding hydrogels with excellent structural integrity, tunable stiffness, and high-resolution DLP printing performance. In vitro, CAA demonstrates excellent cytocompatibility, promoting cell adhesion, proliferation, migration, and 3D encapsulation with high postprinting viability. In a full-thickness diabetic wound model, bioprinted CAA constructs, especially when combined with fibroblasts and keratinocytes, significantly accelerated wound closure, enhanced collagen I/III regeneration, restored elastic fiber integrity, stimulated angiogenesis, and reduced oxidative stress, collectively restoring ECM homeostasis and tissue architecture. Furthermore, the upregulation of regenerative markers, such as Ki67 and EGF, highlights the material's ability to modulate the wound microenvironment and activate endogenous repair pathways. This work establishes CAA as a highly soluble, bioactive, and photoprintable collagen platform with strong potential for precision 3D bioprinting and regenerative therapy of chronic diabetic wounds.

papers.title: BLAC-Q4DIM: a bayesian optimization and LSTM driven adaptive clustering quasi-four-dimensional ionospheric model
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate Slant Total Electron Content (STEC) modeling is essential for high-precision Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning and space-weather monitoring. However, conventional Global Ionospheric Maps (GIMs) and fixed-parameter ionospheric models have limited capability in capturing rapid ionospheric variations associated with geomagnetic disturbances, low-latitude irregularities, and heterogeneous GNSS station distributions. Their performance is constrained by fixed spatial scales and insufficient adaptivity to the dynamic and spatially varying characteristics of the ionosphere. This study proposes BLAC-Q4DIM, an adaptive clustering quasi-four-dimensional ionospheric model driven by Bayesian Optimization (BO) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). It directly clusters STEC in a Four-Dimensional (4D) latitude-longitude-elevation-azimuth domain and integrates four classical algorithms (GRID, KMEANS, DBSCAN, and AGGLO), four robust variants (TKMEANS, DPMEANS, HDBSCAN, and LEIDEN), 15 spatiotemporal features, and three optional geomagnetic drivers within a closed-loop adaptive framework consisting of LSTM prior prediction, BO-based posterior correction, and periodic retraining. Global experiments conducted over two representative 30-day periods, covering geomagnetically quiet and disturbed conditions, demonstrate that BLAC-Q4DIM consistently outperforms the Fixed-Parameter Q4DIM Framework (F-Q) and a GIM baseline. The best-performing variants, HDBSCAN and DPMEANS, achieve Root Mean Square (RMS) errors of 0.96–1.01 Total Electron Content Units (TECU) during the quiet period and 1.34–1.40 TECU during the disturbed period, representing RMS reductions of 80%-85% relative to the GIM baseline and more than 58% relative to the best F-Q baseline. BLAC-Q4DIM also demonstrates strong robustness under low-latitude, station-sparse, and disturbed conditions. The four robust variants maintain RMS errors below 2 TECU at low latitudes and below 1.44 TECU under the sparsest reference-station configuration, while limiting the performance degradation caused by geomagnetic disturbance to only 0.41 TECU. HDBSCAN and DPMEANS require only 3.5 s and 5.9 s, respectively, for single-window LSTM prediction and BO posterior correction, demonstrating the potential for near-real-time ionospheric modeling. These results indicate that BLAC-Q4DIM provides an adaptive, accurate, robust, and efficient framework for STEC modeling, offering a promising solution for next-generation GNSS positioning and space-weather applications.

papers.title: Development of TPMS Lattice Substrates for Catalytic Cracking Applications via Fused Filament Fabrication
papers.abstract: The advancement of catalytic substrates through Additive Manufacturing (AM) offers notable benefits over conventional techniques, particularly for producing intricate three-dimensional forms that enable precise control over pore dimensions and surface characteristics. These attributes play a vital role in improving catalytic efficiency, which is evaluated by measuring pressure drop and mass transfer. This research focuses on the design and manufacture of a monolithic ceramic filter for catalytic cracking. The monoliths under study have a Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) lattice. A macroporosity of about 65% is the criterion used to model the structures, and the TPMS unit cell length is the design parameter to achieve that porosity. Adapting a conventional Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF) desktop to use alumina filament, we produced samples based on three TPMS types: Schwar-Primitive (SP), Schoen Gyroid (SG), and Schwarz-Diamond (SD), which, after a plastic debinding process and subsequent sintering, resulted in meso-scale porous structures. The samples showed relative dimensional errors below 5% and a real total porosity of around 70%, with a maximum difference of 4% among the TPMS types. Because the printed SP lattices have the lowest unit cell length and real porosity, their pressure drop measurements were higher than those of the SG and SD. The opposite occurred with the estimated permeability. Although yielding similar pressure drop results, printed SG lattices had greater permeability than SD; therefore, in terms of monolith fluid dynamics, the SG lattice is the preferred geometry.

papers.title: Predicting the Effect of Chemotherapy on the State of a Cancerous Tumor Using Fractal-Physical-Information Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Understanding tumor dynamics under chemotherapy is important for improving the prediction of cancer progression and assessing treatment effectiveness. This paper proposes a numerical modeling approach based on a fractal physics-informed neural network (fPINN) designed to solve nonlinear fractional-order differential equations describing the interaction of cell populations during cancer therapy. The mathematical model is formulated using the Atangana–Baleanu fractional operator in the Caputo sense, which makes it possible to capture both the fractal structure and hereditary properties of biological systems. The proposed architecture consists of four independent neural networks modeling the concentrations of stem cells, effector cells, tumor cells, and the chemotherapeutic agent. Model training is performed using a hybrid loss function that combines the residuals of the governing equations, initial conditions, and reference data generated by the Atangana–Toufik numerical method. The experimental results demonstrate high model accuracy, particularly for components with complex nonlinear dynamics. These findings indicate that the proposed fPINN framework is a promising tool for predicting tumor evolution and analyzing the impact of chemotherapy.

papers.title: Novel enhancement of fatigue life in steels through extrinsic mechanisms enabled by additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: This study presents a novel additive manufacturing-enabled strategy for enhancing fatigue life in monolithic metals through location-specific extrinsic toughening. Compact tension specimens of 18Ni(300) Maraging steel were fabricated using laser powder bed fusion, incorporating unbonded, dog-bone-shaped ligament features strategically placed along the anticipated crack path. These ligaments remain mechanically inactive until the advancing crack bypasses them, at which point they engage and act as crack-bridging elements, reducing the effective stress intensity at the crack tip. Three ligament types—Rounded-End, Flat-End and Integrated ligaments—were investigated across various diameters to evaluate the influence of geometry on fatigue performance. Experimental fatigue crack growth tests revealed up to 57% local reduction in crack growth rate and fatigue life extension of up to 13%, primarily in rounded-end specimens. Crack closure and bridging were identified as the dominant toughening mechanisms, with early-positioned ligaments proving most effective. Surface roughness of fabricated ligaments emerged as a critical limitation, leading to premature fatigue failure in some designs. The findings demonstrate, for the first time, that geometry-driven location-specific extrinsic toughening can be systematically implemented in a single-phase metal via additive manufacturing, offering a new design tool for localized, architecture-based damage tolerance in structural alloys that cannot be realized through conventional methods.

papers.title: Architecture and collocation sampling of purely physics-informed neural networks for efficient and reliable thermal simulation of wire-arc directed energy deposition
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a promising alternative to computationally demanding finite element (FE) simulations for thermal analysis of large-scale wire-arc directed energy deposition (WA-DED) without requiring labeled data. However, practical application remains hindered by a lack of systematic guidance on network architecture and collocation-point sampling, which strongly influence accuracy, robustness, and computational cost. This study presents a controlled parametric investigation of the two key PINN design choices: (i) the collocation point sample size and distribution, and (ii) the network topology. The thermal problem is governed by the transient heat conduction equation incorporating Goldak's heat source, convection, radiation, and Dirichlet boundary conditions. Fully connected networks (depths of 3–6, widths 8–64) are evaluated using a Sobol-based sampling strategy with locally increased collocation points around the moving heat source. Training across seven random seeds yielded over 1500 trained models, evaluated against a validated FE model. All investigated topologies were sufficiently expressive to achieve RMSE values below 100 K, although variability occurred across sampling configurations and seeds. Increasing near-source collocation density to 2–5 times the background density generally improves accuracy, whereas lower ratios consistently deteriorate performance. When accuracy and computational cost are considered jointly, near-source sampling is not consistently advantageous. 16-wide Networks provide the most favorable balance between accuracy, reliability, and computational efficiency. The best model achieves an RMSE of 42.1 K using 21,355 collocation points in 240 s. These findings provide actionable guidance for PINN design and establish a basis for extending WA-DED thermal simulations toward digital-twin applications.
